Every table row is now satisfiable against its named surface — I re-walked all of them (spec create, spec approve, plan approve with its carve-out, next, all three complete legs, both release legs, terminal rows) and found no remaining row/surface mismatch. findings.title: New R3.6/AC-16 consistency scan: clean, and load-bearing for the sanction boundary
findings.detail: R3.6's premise was verified in my round-4 pass (spec.go:76 writes mindspec_phase=plan unconditionally on the existing-epic path), so the replay-regression fixture is real and AC-16 is red-on-revert as claimed. AC-16's structure is sound: the later-value fixture (implement, variant review) with mutation-vs-no-op output honesty covers both admissible dispositions (absent-only backfill no-op, fail-closed refusal) without foreclosing the plan-time choice, and the separate empty-phase leg keeps the legitimate backfill pinned rather than accidentally outlawed. Cross-requirement consistency: spec.go:76 was already in R3.3's locked-writer inventory, In Scope's spec.go entry now carries R3.6, and — notably — R3.6 is necessary for the round-3 sanction sentence to be true: without it, spec-approve replay is a second unforced backward writer, contradicting 'the sanctioned internal release-sync caller is the ONLY unforced backward writer'. With R3.6 every non-release backward path is either guarded (repair), refused/no-op (spec approve replay), or absent. The output-honesty clause (a replay that changed nothing never claims to have set the phase) also aligns with Goal (a)'s success-never-indistinguishable-from-no-op principle.
